aspect: EXAMPLE - the rate, and that it never moves
description: INEGI recorded informality at 55.1% in Q2 2026, up from 54.8%, with 54.78% in Q1 2026 covering 32.63 million people. The share has been essentially stagnant for two decades and remains above 50%.
energy_note: Twenty years of reform, and the number does not move.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the unemployment rate is a decoy
description: Mexican unemployment was reported at 2.4% - the lowest in the OECD - alongside very high informality and slow formal job growth. Almost everyone works; the question is under what terms.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and a rising share earn at or below minimum
description: Nearly 27.9 million people earn the minimum wage or less - 45.7% of the employed population, an annual increase of 4.3 million. INEGI's critical employment conditions rate rose from 36.3% in May 2025 to 38.7% in May 2026.
energy_note: Nearly half the workforce, at or under the floor.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the wage did rise, substantially
description: The daily minimum wage reached MX$315.04 in most of the country and MX$440.87 in the northern border zone on 1 January 2026, a 13% increase, with the federal minimum up more than 100% in real terms since 2018. This is recorded because it is real and unusual.
energy_note: It genuinely doubled, and it is still this.
